newsitem.title: UK: Labour says UK pension would rise with inflation.
newsitem.headline: Labour says UK pension would rise with inflation.

text.p: Britain's main opposition Labour Party social security spokeswoman Harriet Harman said on Wednesday the current basic state pension would rise in line with inflation under a Labour government.

"The basic state pension will play a key role in achieving our objectives. We are committed to maintaining it - not means tested - as the foundation for security in retirement and it will rise in line with inflation," Harman told the National Association of Pension Funds.
She said an incoming Labour government faced a pensions crisis, with 3.5 million pensioners on income support, and further action was necessary if the problem was to be tackled effectively.

Labour's first priority would be to a million pensioners who do not receive the income support to which they are entitled, establishing a new "Pension Entitlement', which she said would avoid "the stigma and other failings of income support".
"Labour's aim for future generations of pensioners is that they will not have to depend on income related benefits when they retire."
The key to this was extending second tier provision of pensions as widely as possible. This would be done through Labour's "Stakeholder Pension' scheme announced last year.
Labour says the plan would provide better value for money and more security than personal pensions.
The scheme seeks to encourage partnerships between workplace organisations such as unions and employers' organisations, and financial service companies.
